previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, chronic pancreatitis, and long-term anticoagulation was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea following a meal. Evaluation revealed melena and acute on chronic blood loss anemia with hemoglobin dropping to 8.5 g/dL. A CT scan showed biliary duct dilation likely from prior cholecystectomy, and an EGD revealed a gastric ulcer but no active bleeding. She received 3 units of packed red blood cells, with stabilization of her hemoglobin. Warfarin was held initially and later restarted at a lower target INR of 2–2.5 per cardiology recommendation. Her symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home in improved condition with instructions to monitor weight, manage heart failure symptoms, and follow up with her PCP and specialists for ongoing evaluation of anemia, biliary findings, and medication management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with PMHx of ___, AS s/p AVR complicated by 
cardiac arrest, CHB s/p permanent pacemaker, Afib on 
anticoagulation, history of chronic venous insufficiency, 
history of recurrent cellulitis, lipodermatosclerosis, 
presenting with recurrent cellulitis. 

# Lower Extremity Erythema/Swelling/Serous Drainage
Patient presented with bilateral lower extremity erythema, edema 
and areas of serous oozing from areas of skin breakdown most 
consistent with cellulitis. However there was no evidence of 
purulence from the wounds. She remained afebrile, without 
leukocytosis and hemodynamically stable but reportedly had low 
grade fever at home with temperature of 100 with associated 
chills. She was started on IV vancomycin in the ED, which was 
continued on the medicine floor. The differential included 
lipodermatosclerosis, allergic contact dermatitis and 
inflammatory etiologies but these were thought less likely given 
the clinical appearance and improvement with IV Vancomycin. 
Bilateral lower extremity ultrasounds were checked in the ED and 
were negative for DVT, and with evidence of respiratory 
variation in the common femoral arteries. The patient was 
evaluated by wound care but the patient deferred wrapping or 
further interventions. A TSH was checked and was within normal 
limits. A ___ IgA was sent and was normal. The patient had 
previously been on PO Keflex prophylaxis but had not been on it 
recently prior to admission.  ID was consulted for assistance 
with antibiotic management and need for further antibiotic 
prophylaxis moving forward. The patient was continued on IV 
Vancomycin per ID recommendations with clinical improvement. The 
patient was transitioned to PO Keflex on discharge, for a total 
of 10 days of antibiotics, with plans for prophylactic PO Keflex 
after completion of course of antibiotics for ___ acute 
cellulitis. Blood cultures were without growth on discharge. 
Given signs of increased lower extremity edema the patient's 
dose of torsemide was given a 1x dose of 40 mg of torsemide than 
resumed on home 20 mg daily. 
 
# Left Arm Pain
The patient also presented with left forearm pain and allodynia 
previously evaluated by outpatient providers ___. This was 
thought to possibly represent complex regional pain syndrome 
(reflex sympathetic dystrophy) given that the pain is 
disproportionate to clinical findings. ___ symptoms included 
pain and allodynia, as well as possible edema of the forearm 
compartment, though no clear autonomic, trophic or motor 
symptoms currently. An XR of the wrist and forearm was 
consistent with scapholunate advanced collapse (SLAC), as well 
as calcification of the fibrocartilage of the distal ulna, which 
could represent deposition disease such as CPPD, however no 
fracture or dislocation or osteopenia to suggest CRPS noted. The 
patients pain was stable on discharge.

EXAMINATION:  DX FOREARM AND WRIST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with left wrist/forearm pain.  // Please
evaluate for soft tissue injury/fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Left wrist, three views
Left elbow, two views

COMPARISON:  Left wrist and elbow radiographs ___

FINDINGS: 

THREE VIEWS, LEFT WRIST

Compared with radiographs from ___, no significant changes detected. 
Again seen is abnormal widening of the scapholunate interval, measuring 8 mm,
with migration of the capitate, consistent with advanced SLAC wrist.  No
definite fracture or dislocation is seen.  Moderate degenerate change is seen,
most prominent at the first CMC joint and radioscaphoid articulation.  There
is calcification of the triangular fibrocartilage of the distal ulna.  In the
dorsal aspect of the soft tissues of the hand, there is evidence of
heterotopic ossification.  There is relative bony demineralization.

TWO VIEWS, LEFT ELBOW

Again seen is spurring arising off the radial tuberosity.  No fracture
dislocation is identified.  No joint effusion is seen.

IMPRESSION: 

No definite acute fracture or dislocation.  Findings consistent with advanced
SLAC wrist. Moderate degenerative change as described above.  Calcification of
the triangular fibrocartilage of the distal ulna, which could represent
deposition disease such as CPPD.
